docs.title: Cost of indirection
docs.text:
Description. Each abstraction (interface, factory, registry, proxy) adds types and navigation steps between a reader and the behaviour they're looking for. The runtime cost is usually negligible; the cognitive cost is paid every time someone reads, debugs or changes the code. A pattern earns its keep when the variation it enables is real and frequent.

Advantages / features. Thinking about cost makes designs proportionate: direct code where things are stable, patterns where change concentrates.

IndirectionCostDemo.java
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.function.Supplier;

/**
 * Cost of indirection: the same discount rule written directly and through Strategy + Factory + Registry. The
 * patterned version costs more types and a deeper call path for every reader; it pays off only when variants and
 * change make it worth it.
 */
public class IndirectionCostDemo {

    static int depthAtCalculation;
    static void markDepth() { depthAtCalculation = Thread.currentThread().getStackTrace().length; }

    // ----- direct: one method -----
    static long directDiscount(String tier, long totalPaise) {                                     // (1)!
        markDepth();
        return tier.equals("GOLD") ? totalPaise / 10 : 0;
    }

    // ----- patterned: interface, implementations, factory, registry -----
    interface DiscountStrategy { long discount(long totalPaise); }
    static final class GoldDiscount implements DiscountStrategy { public long discount(long t) { markDepth(); return t / 10; } }
    static final class NoDiscount implements DiscountStrategy { public long discount(long t) { markDepth(); return 0; } }
    static final class DiscountRegistry {
        private final Map<String, Supplier<DiscountStrategy>> byTier = new HashMap<>();
        DiscountRegistry register(String tier, Supplier<DiscountStrategy> s) { byTier.put(tier, s); return this; }
        DiscountStrategy forTier(String tier) { return byTier.getOrDefault(tier, NoDiscount::new).get(); }
    }
    static final class DiscountService {
        private final DiscountRegistry registry;
        DiscountService(DiscountRegistry registry) { this.registry = registry; }
        long discount(String tier, long total) { return lookup(tier).discount(total); }            // (2)!
        private DiscountStrategy lookup(String tier) { return registry.forTier(tier); }
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        long d1 = directDiscount("GOLD", 50_000);
        int directDepth = depthAtCalculation;
        DiscountService service = new DiscountService(new DiscountRegistry().register("GOLD", GoldDiscount::new));
        long d2 = service.discount("GOLD", 50_000);
        int patternedDepth = depthAtCalculation;

        System.out.println("same answer: " + (d1 == d2) + " (Rs " + d1 / 100 + ")");
        System.out.println("types to read: direct 0, patterned 5 (interface, 2 strategies, registry, service)");
        System.out.println("runtime cost: " + (patternedDepth - directDepth) + " extra stack frame (negligible)");
        System.out.println("reader cost: direct 1 jump to the rule; patterned 5 (service, lookup, registry, registration, strategy)");
        System.out.println("to add a PLATINUM tier: direct = edit 1 method; patterned = add 1 class + 1 registration");   // (3)!
    }
}
  1. The direct version: the rule is where you'd look for it.
  2. The patterned version routes through a service, a lookup, a registry and a strategy.
  3. The benefit appears only when variants are added: a new class instead of editing a method.

Run it: java IndirectionCostDemo.java

same answer: true (Rs 50)
types to read: direct 0, patterned 5 (interface, 2 strategies, registry, service)
runtime cost: 1 extra stack frame (negligible)
reader cost: direct 1 jump to the rule; patterned 5 (service, lookup, registry, registration, strategy)
to add a PLATINUM tier: direct = edit 1 method; patterned = add 1 class + 1 registration
Indirection pays off when It doesn't when Several variants exist now "We might need it one day" Variants change independently, often The code changes once a year Different teams own variants One person owns all of it Variants need isolated tests A single table test covers everything A seam is needed for a volatile dependency The dependency is stable (the JDK)

Use patterns where change concentrates. Avoid speculative generality ("YAGNI"). Real-world Java: Spring's own code is heavily layered because it's a framework with thousands of extension needs; your application usually isn't. Best practice: state the variation a pattern absorbs in its Javadoc or ADR. Gotcha: removing a pattern later is also a cost; prefer adding it late over adding it early.

docs.title: Decision frameworks
docs.text:
Description. Structured ways to choose: list options, agree the criteria and their weights with the team before scoring, score, and then test sensitivity (does a small weight change flip the result?). For recurring decisions, write explicit thresholds (e.g. "three or more variants changing monthly → Strategy").

Advantages / features. Disagreements move from taste to forces and weights; close calls are visible as close; decisions are explainable later.

DecisionMatrixDemo.java
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

/**
 * A weighted decision matrix: score options against criteria the team agreed on, then check sensitivity: if a
 * small change in weights flips the winner, the decision is close and the trade-off needs discussion, not maths.
 */
public class DecisionMatrixDemo {

    record Option(String name, Map<String, Integer> scores) {}                                     // scores 1..5

    static String winner(List<Option> options, Map<String, Integer> weights, Map<String, Integer> totalsOut) {
        totalsOut.clear();
        for (Option o : options) {
            int total = 0;
            for (var w : weights.entrySet()) total += w.getValue() * o.scores().get(w.getKey());       // (1)!
            totalsOut.put(o.name(), total);
        }
        return totalsOut.entrySet().stream().max(Map.Entry.comparingByValue()).get().getKey();
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<Option> options = List.of(
                new Option("enum + switch", Map.of("simplicity", 5, "add-a-rule", 2, "testability", 3, "runtime-config", 1)),
                new Option("Strategy beans", Map.of("simplicity", 3, "add-a-rule", 4, "testability", 5, "runtime-config", 2)),
                new Option("rules engine", Map.of("simplicity", 1, "add-a-rule", 5, "testability", 3, "runtime-config", 5)));
        Map<String, Integer> weights = new LinkedHashMap<>();                                       // (2)!
        weights.put("simplicity", 3); weights.put("add-a-rule", 3); weights.put("testability", 2); weights.put("runtime-config", 1);

        Map<String, Integer> totals = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        System.out.println("baseline winner: " + winner(options, weights, totals) + " " + totals);
        for (String criterion : weights.keySet()) {                                                 // (3)!
            Map<String, Integer> nudged = new LinkedHashMap<>(weights);
            nudged.merge(criterion, 2, Integer::sum);
            String w = winner(options, nudged, totals);
            System.out.println("  if " + criterion + " weighs +2: " + w + (w.equals("Strategy beans") ? "" : "  <- flips"));
        }
    }
}
  1. Each option's score is the weighted sum over the agreed criteria.
  2. Weights are agreed before scoring, so they can't be tuned to a favourite.
  3. Nudging each weight shows which criterion the decision hinges on.

Run it: java DecisionMatrixDemo.java

baseline winner: Strategy beans {enum + switch=28, Strategy beans=33, rules engine=29}
  if simplicity weighs +2: Strategy beans
  if add-a-rule weighs +2: Strategy beans
  if testability weighs +2: Strategy beans
  if runtime-config weighs +2: rules engine  <- flips
Framework Good for Weighted decision matrix Comparing 2–5 options on several criteria Explicit thresholds / heuristics Recurring choices (when to extract a Strategy) ATAM-style quality scenarios Architecture-level trade-offs (latency vs consistency) Cost of delay / reversibility How long to spend deciding Spike / prototype When scores are guesses

Use for decisions with several plausible options and real consequences. Avoid false precision: scores are opinions; the value is in the discussion and the sensitivity check. Real-world Java: choosing between Spring Data JPA, jOOQ and plain JDBC; between Kafka and RabbitMQ; between Strategy beans and a rules engine. Best practice: write the losing options and why they lost into the ADR. Gotcha: a decision that flips on one weight isn't decided by the matrix; it's decided by whoever sets that weight, so discuss that criterion explicitly.

docs.title: Architecture Decision Records
docs.text:
Description. An ADR is a short markdown file in the repository: number, title, status (Proposed, Accepted, Deprecated, Superseded), context (forces), decision, consequences (good and bad). ADRs are immutable once accepted; when a decision changes, a new ADR supersedes the old one, and both remain.

Advantages / features. New team members learn why, not just what; decisions are reviewed like code; superseding preserves history.

AdrDemo.java
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * Architecture Decision Records: short, numbered, immutable documents (context, decision, consequences, status).
 * Decisions aren't edited when they change; a new ADR supersedes the old one, so the history stays readable.
 */
public class AdrDemo {

    record Adr(int number, String title, String status, String context, String decision, String consequences, Integer supersedes) {
        String toMarkdown() {                                                                        // (1)!
            return "# ADR-" + String.format("%04d", number) + ": " + title + "\n\n"
                    + "Status: " + status + (supersedes == null ? "" : " (supersedes ADR-" + String.format("%04d", supersedes) + ")") + "\n\n"
                    + "## Context\n" + context + "\n\n## Decision\n" + decision + "\n\n## Consequences\n" + consequences + "\n";
        }
    }

    static List<Adr> supersede(List<Adr> log, int old, Adr replacement) {                          // (2)!
        List<Adr> next = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Adr a : log)
            next.add(a.number() == old ? new Adr(a.number(), a.title(), "Superseded by ADR-" + String.format("%04d", replacement.number()),
                    a.context(), a.decision(), a.consequences(), a.supersedes()) : a);
        next.add(replacement);
        return next;
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<Adr> log = List.of(new Adr(7, "Delivery fees as an enum switch", "Accepted",
                "Three fee rules, changed twice a year.", "Use an enum with a switch in DeliveryFeeCalculator.",
                "Simple; adding a rule needs a deploy.", null));
        Adr adr12 = new Adr(12, "Delivery fees as Strategy beans", "Accepted",
                "Eleven fee rules, city teams change them weekly.", "One Strategy bean per rule, selected by city and slot.",
                "Rules testable in isolation; one more indirection; enum removed.", 7);
        log = supersede(log, 7, adr12);
        System.out.print(adr12.toMarkdown());
        System.out.println();
        log.forEach(a -> System.out.println("ADR-" + String.format("%04d", a.number()) + " " + a.title() + " [" + a.status() + "]"));   // (3)!
    }
}
  1. Nygard's template: title, status, context, decision, consequences.
  2. Changing a decision means a new ADR and a status change on the old one, never editing it.
  3. The log shows the whole history at a glance.

Run it: java AdrDemo.java

# ADR-0012: Delivery fees as Strategy beans

Status: Accepted (supersedes ADR-0007)

## Context
Eleven fee rules, city teams change them weekly.

## Decision
One Strategy bean per rule, selected by city and slot.

## Consequences
Rules testable in isolation; one more indirection; enum removed.

ADR-0007 Delivery fees as an enum switch [Superseded by ADR-0012]
ADR-0012 Delivery fees as Strategy beans [Accepted]
ADR practice Why One decision per ADR Easy to supersede precisely Keep in the repo (docs/adr/) Reviewed in PRs; versioned with code Consequences include the downsides Honest trade-offs build trust Optional Review-by date Forces a revisit when assumptions may expire Cite ADR numbers in code comments Readers find the reasoning

Use for decisions that are costly to reverse, cross team boundaries, or will surprise future readers. Avoid ADRs for every library bump; that buries the important ones. Real-world Java: adr-tools, Log4brains, MADR template; ADR folders in many open-source Java projects. Best practice: write the ADR before or with the code change, in the same PR. Gotcha: editing an accepted ADR rewrites history; supersede it instead.

docs.title: Reversibility
docs.text:
Description. Estimate how expensive it would be to undo a decision: code touched, teams involved, data migrations, external contracts. Two-way doors (cheap to reverse) should be decided quickly and revisited with data; one-way doors (published schemas, data models, vendor lock-in) deserve prototypes, ADRs and review. Seams (ports, adapters, feature flags) convert some one-way doors into two-way ones at small cost.

Advantages / features. Effort goes where mistakes are expensive; teams move fast on everything else.

ReversibilityDemo.java
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.TreeMap;

/**
 * Reversibility: classify decisions as one-way or two-way doors by what it would cost to undo them, and buy
 * reversibility cheaply where it matters with a seam (an interface) at the boundary.
 */
public class ReversibilityDemo {

    record Decision(String name, int filesTouchedToUndo, int teamsInvolved, boolean dataMigration, boolean externalContract) {
        int reversalCost() { return filesTouchedToUndo * teamsInvolved * (dataMigration ? 5 : 1) * (externalContract ? 3 : 1); }   // (1)!
        String door() { return reversalCost() >= 100 ? "one-way door: slow down, write an ADR, prototype" : "two-way door: decide fast, revisit later"; }
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<String> sources = List.of(
                "CheckoutService: PayLinkClient.charge(...)", "RefundService: PayLinkClient.refund(...)",
                "SubscriptionBilling: PayLinkClient.mandate(...)", "WalletTopUp: PayLinkClient.charge(...)",
                "AdminTools: PayLinkClient.lookup(...)", "Reconciliation: PayLinkClient.settlements(...)");
        System.out.println("PayLink calls spread through the code: " + sources.size() + " files to change to switch provider");
        System.out.println("behind a PaymentGateway port: 1 adapter file to change");                // (2)!

        Map<String, String> verdicts = new TreeMap<>();
        for (Decision d : List.of(
                new Decision("Caffeine vs Guava cache inside pricing", 2, 1, false, false),
                new Decision("PayLink SDK called directly everywhere", 6, 4, true, false),
                new Decision("Event schema published to 4 teams", 8, 5, true, true),
                new Decision("Payment provider behind a port", 1, 1, true, false)))
            verdicts.put(d.name(), "cost " + d.reversalCost() + ": " + d.door());                    // (3)!
        verdicts.forEach((k, v) -> System.out.println(k + " -> " + v));
    }
}
  1. A rough reversal-cost model: files, teams, data migration and external contracts multiply.
  2. A port concentrates the vendor dependency in one adapter.
  3. The same choice (PayLink) is a one-way door when spread through the code and a two-way door behind a port.

Run it: java ReversibilityDemo.java

PayLink calls spread through the code: 6 files to change to switch provider
behind a PaymentGateway port: 1 adapter file to change
Caffeine vs Guava cache inside pricing -> cost 2: two-way door: decide fast, revisit later
Event schema published to 4 teams -> cost 600: one-way door: slow down, write an ADR, prototype
PayLink SDK called directly everywhere -> cost 120: one-way door: slow down, write an ADR, prototype
Payment provider behind a port -> cost 5: two-way door: decide fast, revisit later
Usually one-way Usually two-way Published API and event schemas Internal class structure Database schema with data In-process library choice behind a facade Choice of primary datastore Cache provider Public URLs, identifiers Feature implementations behind flags Contracts with vendors Build tooling

Use reversibility to decide how much process a decision needs. Avoid treating everything as one-way (paralysis) or everything as two-way (expensive surprises). Real-world Java: hexagonal ports for payment and messaging providers, feature flags, expand-and-contract schema migrations. Best practice: for one-way doors, look for a way to make them two-way first. Gotcha: seams have a cost too; don't wrap stable dependencies just in case.

docs.title: Example 1: Minimal (L2)
docs.text:
Scenario: FreshCart's delivery-fee rules grew one at a time over a year.

RuleOfThreeDemo.java
/** Minimal: don't introduce a pattern for one case; tolerate two; extract when the third variant arrives. */
public class RuleOfThreeDemo {

    static String advice(int variants) {
        if (variants <= 1) return "write it inline; no abstraction yet";                            // (1)!
        if (variants == 2) return "an if/else is fine; note the duplication";
        return "extract an abstraction (e.g. Strategy) now that the variation is real";               // (2)!
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        String[] history = {"Mon: flat Rs 25 delivery fee", "Mar: free above Rs 199", "Jun: Rs 10 off for DairyDay subscribers"};
        for (int i = 0; i < history.length; i++) System.out.println(history[i] + " -> " + advice(i + 1));
    }
}
  1. One case: no abstraction.
  2. The third variant is the signal that the variation is real.

Run it: java RuleOfThreeDemo.java

Output:

Mon: flat Rs 25 delivery fee -> write it inline; no abstraction yet
Mar: free above Rs 199 -> an if/else is fine; note the duplication
Jun: Rs 10 off for DairyDay subscribers -> extract an abstraction (e.g. Strategy) now that the variation is real

What to notice:

  • Extracting at the third case means the abstraction is shaped by three real examples, not one guess.

docs.title: Example 2: Realistic (in FreshCart grocery delivery)
docs.text:
Scenario: the same delivery-fee design was reviewed three times as the business grew. The reviewer recorded forces, not opinions.

DeliveryFeeReviewDemo.java
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * Realistic: a design review for FreshCart's delivery-fee rules. Instead of arguing taste, the reviewer records the
 * forces (variants, change rate, who changes them, need for runtime changes) and applies explicit thresholds, so
 * the recommendation and its reasons can go straight into an ADR.
 */
public class DeliveryFeeReviewDemo {

    record Forces(int variants, int changesPerMonth, int teamsEditing, boolean businessEditsWithoutDeploy) {}
    record Recommendation(String design, List<String> reasons) {}

    static Recommendation review(Forces f) {
        List<String> reasons = new ArrayList<>();
        if (f.businessEditsWithoutDeploy()) {                                                         // (1)!
            reasons.add("business must change rules without a deploy");
            if (f.variants() > 20) reasons.add(f.variants() + " rules: a table-driven or rules-engine approach scales better than classes");
            return new Recommendation(f.variants() > 20 ? "rules engine / decision table" : "rules as data in config", reasons);
        }
        if (f.variants() >= 3 && (f.changesPerMonth() >= 2 || f.teamsEditing() > 1)) {               // (2)!
            reasons.add(f.variants() + " variants changing " + f.changesPerMonth() + "x a month");
            if (f.teamsEditing() > 1) reasons.add(f.teamsEditing() + " teams edit rules: separate classes avoid merge conflicts");
            return new Recommendation("Strategy per rule, selected by a small registry", reasons);
        }
        reasons.add("few variants (" + f.variants() + "), rarely changed (" + f.changesPerMonth() + "x a month)");
        return new Recommendation("keep the enum + switch; revisit at the next variant", reasons);     // (3)!
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Forces[] snapshots = {
                new Forces(3, 0, 1, false),
                new Forces(11, 4, 3, false),
                new Forces(40, 30, 1, true)};
        String[] when = {"2025 Q1", "2026 Q2", "2026 Q4 proposal"};
        for (int i = 0; i < snapshots.length; i++) {
            Recommendation r = review(snapshots[i]);
            System.out.println(when[i] + ": " + r.design());
            r.reasons().forEach(reason -> System.out.println("    because " + reason));
        }
    }
}
  1. Who changes the rules, and whether they need a deploy, is checked first: it changes the whole category of solution.
  2. Thresholds for moving to Strategy: enough variants and enough change or ownership spread.
  3. Below the thresholds, the simple design stays, with a stated trigger to revisit.

Run it: java DeliveryFeeReviewDemo.java

Output:

2025 Q1: keep the enum + switch; revisit at the next variant
    because few variants (3), rarely changed (0x a month)
2026 Q2: Strategy per rule, selected by a small registry
    because 11 variants changing 4x a month
    because 3 teams edit rules: separate classes avoid merge conflicts
2026 Q4 proposal: rules engine / decision table
    because business must change rules without a deploy
    because 40 rules: a table-driven or rules-engine approach scales better than classes

What to notice:

  • The right answer changed twice, and each answer was right at its time.
  • The reasons print in a form that drops straight into an ADR's Context section.

docs.title: Example 3: Production-grade
docs.text:
Scenario: FreshCart keeps ADRs in docs/adr/. A CI step keeps them trustworthy: valid structure, valid links, reviews not forgotten, and no code citing decisions that have been replaced.

AdrLogDemo.java
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.TreeMap;
import java.util.regex.Matcher;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

/**
 * Production-grade: a CI check for FreshCart's ADR folder. It parses ADR files, validates their structure and links,
 * flags decisions past their review date, finds code that still cites superseded ADRs, and prints an index.
 */
public class AdrLogDemo {

    record Adr(int number, String title, String status, Integer supersededBy, LocalDate reviewBy, Set<String> sections) {}

    static final Pattern HEADER = Pattern.compile("^# ADR-(\\d{4}): (.+)$", Pattern.MULTILINE);
    static final Pattern STATUS = Pattern.compile("^Status: (Proposed|Accepted|Deprecated|Superseded by ADR-(\\d{4}))$", Pattern.MULTILINE);
    static final Pattern REVIEW = Pattern.compile("^Review-by: (\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2})$", Pattern.MULTILINE);
    static final Pattern SECTION = Pattern.compile("^## (\\w+)$", Pattern.MULTILINE);
    static final Set<String> REQUIRED = Set.of("Context", "Decision", "Consequences");

    static Adr parse(String file, String text, List<String> problems) {                               // (1)!
        Matcher h = HEADER.matcher(text), s = STATUS.matcher(text), r = REVIEW.matcher(text), sec = SECTION.matcher(text);
        if (!h.find()) { problems.add(file + ": missing '# ADR-NNNN: title' header"); return null; }
        if (!s.find()) { problems.add(file + ": missing or unknown Status"); return null; }
        Set<String> sections = new java.util.TreeSet<>();
        while (sec.find()) sections.add(sec.group(1));
        for (String required : REQUIRED) if (!sections.contains(required)) problems.add(file + ": missing section '" + required + "'");
        return new Adr(Integer.parseInt(h.group(1)), h.group(2), s.group(1).startsWith("Superseded") ? "Superseded" : s.group(1),
                s.group(2) == null ? null : Integer.parseInt(s.group(2)), r.find() ? LocalDate.parse(r.group(1)) : null, sections);
    }

    static List<String> check(Map<String, String> adrFiles, Map<String, String> sourceFiles, LocalDate today, Map<Integer, Adr> indexOut) {
        List<String> problems = new ArrayList<>();
        adrFiles.forEach((file, text) -> { Adr a = parse(file, text, problems); if (a != null) indexOut.put(a.number(), a); });
        for (Adr a : indexOut.values()) {
            if (a.supersededBy() != null && !indexOut.containsKey(a.supersededBy()))                  // (2)!
                problems.add("ADR-" + id(a.number()) + ": superseded by missing ADR-" + id(a.supersededBy()));
            if (a.status().equals("Accepted") && a.reviewBy() != null && a.reviewBy().isBefore(today))   // (3)!
                problems.add("ADR-" + id(a.number()) + ": review was due " + a.reviewBy());
        }
        Pattern cite = Pattern.compile("ADR-(\\d{4})");
        sourceFiles.forEach((file, code) -> {                                                         // (4)!
            Matcher m = cite.matcher(code);
            while (m.find()) {
                Adr cited = indexOut.get(Integer.parseInt(m.group(1)));
                if (cited == null) problems.add(file + ": cites unknown ADR-" + m.group(1));
                else if (cited.status().equals("Superseded"))
                    problems.add(file + ": cites superseded ADR-" + m.group(1) + "; see ADR-" + id(cited.supersededBy()));
            }
        });
        return problems;
    }

    static String id(int n) { return String.format("%04d", n); }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Map<String, String> adrs = new TreeMap<>();
        adrs.put("0007-delivery-fee-enum.md", "# ADR-0007: Delivery fees as an enum switch\nStatus: Superseded by ADR-0012\n## Context\n.\n## Decision\n.\n## Consequences\n.\n");
        adrs.put("0009-outbox.md", "# ADR-0009: Transactional outbox for order events\nStatus: Accepted\nReview-by: 2026-06-30\n## Context\n.\n## Decision\n.\n## Consequences\n.\n");
        adrs.put("0012-delivery-fee-strategies.md", "# ADR-0012: Delivery fees as Strategy beans\nStatus: Accepted\nReview-by: 2027-06-30\n## Context\n.\n## Decision\n.\n## Consequences\n.\n");
        adrs.put("0013-cache-provider.md", "# ADR-0013: Caffeine as L1 cache\nStatus: Proposed\n## Context\n.\n## Decision\n.\n");
        adrs.put("0014-sms.md", "# ADR-0014: TextBlast as SMS provider\nStatus: Superseded by ADR-0015\n## Context\n.\n## Decision\n.\n## Consequences\n.\n");
        Map<String, String> sources = new TreeMap<>(Map.of(
                "DeliveryFeeCalculator.java", "// Rules live in an enum, see ADR-0007\nenum FeeRule { FLAT, FREE_ABOVE_199 }",
                "OrderEventsPublisher.java", "// Outbox relay per ADR-0009",
                "OtpSender.java", "// Provider choice: ADR-0021"));

        Map<Integer, Adr> index = new TreeMap<>();
        List<String> problems = check(adrs, sources, LocalDate.of(2026, 11, 1), index);
        System.out.println("index:");
        index.values().forEach(a -> System.out.println("  ADR-" + id(a.number()) + " " + a.title() + " [" + a.status() + "]"));   // (5)!
        System.out.println(problems.size() + " problems:");
        problems.forEach(p -> System.out.println("  " + p));
    }
}
  1. Parse each ADR file and check required sections and a known status.
  2. A superseded ADR must point to an ADR that exists.
  3. Accepted decisions with a passed review date are flagged.
  4. Code comments citing superseded or unknown ADRs are flagged with the replacement.
  5. An index of all decisions and statuses is printed for the docs site.

Run it: java AdrLogDemo.java

Output:

index:
  ADR-0007 Delivery fees as an enum switch [Superseded]
  ADR-0009 Transactional outbox for order events [Accepted]
  ADR-0012 Delivery fees as Strategy beans [Accepted]
  ADR-0013 Caffeine as L1 cache [Proposed]
  ADR-0014 TextBlast as SMS provider [Superseded]
5 problems:
  0013-cache-provider.md: missing section 'Consequences'
  ADR-0009: review was due 2026-06-30
  ADR-0014: superseded by missing ADR-0015
  DeliveryFeeCalculator.java: cites superseded ADR-0007; see ADR-0012
  OtpSender.java: cites unknown ADR-0021

What to notice:

  • DeliveryFeeCalculator still claims to follow ADR-0007, which was replaced; the check tells the reader where the current decision is.
  • The outbox decision's review date passed in June; the check prompts a revisit rather than letting assumptions silently expire.
  • In CI, a non-empty problem list fails the build (or posts a warning, for review dates).

docs.title: 7. Pros, Cons & Trade-offs
docs.text: Practice Pros Cons Counting indirection cost Proportionate designs Hard to quantify precisely Decision matrices Explicit trade-offs, sensitivity False precision if misused Explicit thresholds Fast, consistent recurring decisions Thresholds need revisiting ADRs Durable reasoning, onboarding Writing discipline; can become bureaucracy Reversibility analysis Effort where it matters Estimates are rough

docs.title: 8. When to Use / When NOT to Use
docs.text:
Use these practices when:

  • a decision affects several teams or is expensive to reverse;
  • the team disagrees and needs a shared basis;
  • you're reviewing designs for many teams.

Don't when:

  • the decision is cheap to reverse and local (just decide);
  • the matrix would be built to justify a decision already made;
  • ADRs would document trivia.

docs.title: 9. Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Prefer the simplest design that handles today's real variation. (Consensus.)
  2. Extract patterns at the third real variant (rule of three). (Widely used heuristic.)
  3. Agree criteria and weights before scoring options. (Consensus.)
  4. Record significant decisions as ADRs in the repo, with downsides. (Consensus.)
  5. Supersede, don't edit, accepted ADRs. (Consensus.)
  6. Match process to reversibility. (Consensus.)
  7. Add seams around volatile external dependencies, not stable ones. (Consensus.)

docs.title: 10. Pitfalls & Anti-Patterns
docs.text:
Pattern-driven design (production failure mode)

Symptom: a simple delivery-fee change took a week and touched 9 files; incident fixes were slow because nobody could find the rule. Root cause: Strategy, Factory, Registry and Decorator layers added for a rule set that had one variant and changed once a year. Fix: inline the abstraction, keep one seam at the module boundary, and set thresholds for when to reintroduce patterns.

Decisions without records

Symptom: a team removed a "pointless" outbox table and lost events in production. Root cause: the reason for the outbox lived only in a departed engineer's head. Fix: ADRs cited from code; CI flags citations of superseded or unknown ADRs.

Matrix theatre

Symptom: every evaluation recommends the architect's favourite technology. Root cause: weights adjusted after scoring. Fix: fix weights first, publish the sensitivity check, include dissent in the ADR.

Everything is a one-way door

Symptom: months of design reviews for a cache library choice. Root cause: no distinction between reversible and irreversible decisions. Fix: time-box two-way doors; reserve heavy process for one-way doors.

docs.title: 11. Configuration & Tuning
docs.text: Setting Typical value What it does When to change it Risk of changing ADR folder docs/adr/ Where ADRs live Monorepos: per service Hard to find if scattered ADR template Nygard or MADR Required sections Add "Options considered" Longer ADRs get skipped Review-by period 12–24 months Prompts a revisit Fast-moving areas: shorter Review fatigue Extraction threshold 3 variants When to introduce Strategy Higher for stable domains Duplication lingers Reversal-cost threshold Team-defined One-way door process Calibrate with past incidents Too low: paralysis

docs.title: 12. Security Considerations
docs.text:
• Security-relevant decisions (crypto choices, auth flows, data retention) should always get ADRs with explicit threat assumptions and review dates.
  • ADRs must not contain secrets, internal hostnames or vulnerability details that shouldn't be in the repo.
  • Reversibility matters for security: a hard-coded crypto algorithm is a one-way door; design for crypto agility.

docs.title: 13. Performance & Scalability
docs.text: Indirection rarely matters for runtime performance (the JIT inlines monomorphic calls), but it matters for team throughput: time to understand, change and debug. Decision practices scale an organisation: explicit thresholds and ADRs let many teams make consistent choices without a central bottleneck.

docs.title: 14. Testing It
docs.text:
Test decision tooling like any other code, especially when it runs in CI:

AdrLogTest.java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.TreeMap;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

class AdrLogTest {

    static final LocalDate TODAY = LocalDate.of(2026, 11, 1);
    static final String BODY = "## Context\n.\n## Decision\n.\n## Consequences\n.\n";

    static List<String> check(Map<String, String> adrs, Map<String, String> sources) {
        return AdrLogDemo.check(new TreeMap<>(adrs), new TreeMap<>(sources), TODAY, new TreeMap<>());
    }

    @Test
    void wellFormedLogHasNoProblems() {
        var adrs = Map.of("1.md", "# ADR-0001: Use Java 21\nStatus: Accepted\nReview-by: 2027-01-01\n" + BODY);
        assertEquals(List.of(), check(adrs, Map.of("A.java", "// see ADR-0001")));
    }

    @Test
    void missingRequiredSectionIsReported() {
        var problems = check(Map.of("1.md", "# ADR-0001: X\nStatus: Accepted\n## Context\n.\n## Decision\n.\n"), Map.of());
        assertEquals(List.of("1.md: missing section 'Consequences'"), problems);
    }

    @Test
    void unknownStatusIsRejected() {
        var problems = check(Map.of("1.md", "# ADR-0001: X\nStatus: Maybe\n" + BODY), Map.of());
        assertTrue(problems.get(0).contains("missing or unknown Status"));
    }

    @Test
    void danglingSupersededLinkIsReported() {
        var problems = check(Map.of("1.md", "# ADR-0001: X\nStatus: Superseded by ADR-0009\n" + BODY), Map.of());
        assertEquals(List.of("ADR-0001: superseded by missing ADR-0009"), problems);
    }

    @Test
    void overdueReviewOnlyForAcceptedDecisions() {
        var problems = check(Map.of(
                "1.md", "# ADR-0001: X\nStatus: Accepted\nReview-by: 2026-01-01\n" + BODY,
                "2.md", "# ADR-0002: Y\nStatus: Deprecated\nReview-by: 2026-01-01\n" + BODY), Map.of());
        assertEquals(List.of("ADR-0001: review was due 2026-01-01"), problems);
    }

    @Test
    void codeCitingSupersededAdrPointsToReplacement() {
        var problems = check(Map.of(
                "1.md", "# ADR-0001: Old\nStatus: Superseded by ADR-0002\n" + BODY,
                "2.md", "# ADR-0002: New\nStatus: Accepted\n" + BODY), Map.of("Fee.java", "// ADR-0001"));
        assertEquals(List.of("Fee.java: cites superseded ADR-0001; see ADR-0002"), problems);
    }
}

docs.title: 15. Observability & Operations
docs.text: Track ADRs by status and age, overdue reviews, and code citations of superseded ADRs. Watch delivery metrics (lead time for changes, change failure rate) for areas with heavy abstraction; slow changes in a module are a signal to revisit its patterns.

docs.title: 16. Version Notes
docs.text: Year Change 1999 Fowler's Refactoring: rule of three, speculative generality smell 2000 SEI's ATAM for architecture trade-off analysis 2011 Michael Nygard, "Documenting Architecture Decisions" 2016 Bezos letter: "Type 1 and Type 2 decisions" (one-way and two-way doors) 2017 MADR (Markdown ADR) template 2020s ADRs adopted by many engineering orgs; tooling like Log4brains

docs.title: 17. Expert Deep Dive
docs.text:
• Options thinking. Some abstractions are options: you pay a small premium (a seam) for the right to change later. Value them by volatility and cost of change.
  • Last responsible moment. Delay decisions until the cost of not deciding exceeds the value of waiting for more information.
  • Architecture as a set of decisions. Kruchten and Bosch framed architecture as decisions plus rationale; ADRs operationalise that view.
  • Socio-technical forces. Team boundaries and ownership often decide patterns more than technical forces do (Conway).
  • Kill criteria. For experiments, decide upfront what result would make you reverse the decision.

War story: the nine-file fee change

A well-meaning FreshCart engineer designed delivery fees with Strategy, Abstract Factory, a registry and a decorator chain "for future flexibility" when there was one fee rule. Two years later the rule had changed twice, both times by people unfamiliar with the design, and each change took a week. During a pricing incident, on-call engineers needed 40 minutes to find where the fee was actually computed. Fixes: the layers were collapsed into a single calculator with a table test; an ADR recorded the thresholds for reintroducing Strategy; when the third and fourth rules arrived a year later, the team extracted Strategy in a day, shaped by real cases. Lesson: flexibility you don't use is pure cost; add it when the variation shows up.

docs.title: 18. Interview Corner
19. Practice
docs.text:
• Find one abstraction in your codebase with a single implementation and decide whether it's a seam worth keeping. ??? tip "Hint" Is the dependency behind it volatile or external?
  • Write an ADR for a decision your team made last month. ??? tip "Hint" Include the options you rejected and the downsides you accepted.
  • Run a decision matrix with your team and do the sensitivity check together. ??? tip "Hint" Agree weights before anyone scores.
  • Classify your last five architecture decisions as one-way or two-way doors. ??? tip "Hint" Count teams, data and external contracts affected.

docs.title: 20. Quick Revision Card
docs.text:
Remember in 30 seconds

  • Patterns cost readers every day; use them where variation is real.
  • Rule of three; no speculative generality.
  • Agree criteria and weights first; check sensitivity.
  • ADRs: context, decision, consequences, status; supersede, don't edit; cite from code.
  • One-way doors get care; two-way doors get speed; seams make doors two-way.
if (variants >= 3 && (changesPerMonth >= 2 || teamsEditing > 1)) return "Strategy";
return "keep it simple; revisit at the next variant";

  • Martin Fowler, Refactoring (2nd ed., 2018), "Speculative Generality".

docs.title: Projects
docs.text:
TL;DR

Hands-on projects that combine many patterns. The main one is the FreshCart capstone: six milestones from a domain model to production hardening, with a runnable reference solution and tests.

docs.title: Why projects
docs.text: Reading about one pattern at a time teaches the shapes. Combining them teaches the judgement: which pattern earns its place, how they interact (a Decorator around an Adapter behind a Facade), and where the trade-offs land. The capstone uses the same FreshCart domain as every page, so you can jump back to the deep dive for any piece.

docs.title: Project list
docs.text: Project Levels Time Patterns Capstone: FreshCart L1 to L5 6 to 20 hours Value objects, State, Strategy, Specification, Decorator, Adapter, Factory, circuit breaker, Facade, saga, outbox, idempotency key, Observer, aggregator

docs.title: Smaller project ideas
docs.text:
Each of these fits in an evening and reuses the examples from the level pages:

Idea Start from Notification service with SMS, push and email channels, retries and templates Bridge, Template Method, Resilience Patterns Coupon rules engine with a small expression language Interpreter, Specification Undoable cart editor for the mobile app Command, Memento Supplier price feed with routing and dead letters Messaging Patterns Plugin-based delivery partner SDK Designing Frameworks and Libraries

docs.title: How to work through a project
docs.text:
1. Read the milestone and write down which patterns you think fit, and why.
  2. Build the smallest version that passes the acceptance checks.
  3. Write the tests before comparing with the reference solution.
  4. Compare, then note one thing you'd keep from yours and one from the reference.
  5. Run bash examples/run-all.sh to see that every example, including the capstone, still produces its documented output.

docs.title: Capstone: FreshCart
docs.text:
⏱ 6 to 20 hours to build · Prerequisites: L1 and L2 for milestones 1 to 2, L3 and L4 for milestones 3 to 6

TL;DR

Build FreshCart, a grocery delivery backend and its mobile client contract, using most patterns in this playbook. You work through six milestones: domain model, pricing, delivery partners, checkout with saga, outbox and idempotency, the mobile contract, and production hardening. Each milestone lists requirements, the patterns to use and acceptance tests. A runnable one-file reference solution and its JUnit tests are included so you can compare.

docs.title: The product
docs.text:
FreshCart delivers groceries in Bengaluru and Pune within two hours. Customers order from a mobile app; products come from suppliers such as DairyDay and GreenValley; deliveries go through partners QuickDrop (Bengaluru) and ParcelGo (Pune); payments go through PayLink; SMS goes through TextBlast.

flowchart LR
    APP["Mobile app"] --> BFF["Home screen and checkout API"]
    BFF --> CHECKOUT["Checkout facade"]
    CHECKOUT --> PRICING["Pricing: fee strategy, coupons"]
    CHECKOUT --> STOCK["Stock reservations"]
    CHECKOUT --> PAY["PayLink adapter"]
    CHECKOUT --> ROUTER["Partner router and circuit breaker"]
    ROUTER --> QD["QuickDrop adapter"]
    ROUTER --> PG["ParcelGo adapter"]
    CHECKOUT --> OUTBOX[("Outbox")]
    OUTBOX --> RELAY["Relay"]
    RELAY --> SMS["TextBlast notifier"]
    RELAY --> LOYALTY["Loyalty points"]

docs.title: M1: Domain model (L1 to L2)
docs.text:
Build: Money and Product value objects, a Line with a quantity invariant (1 to 20), and an Order aggregate whose lifecycle is Placed → Paid → Dispatched, or Cancelled from Placed or Paid.

Patterns: value objects with records (DDD Tactical), State with a sealed interface, Builder optional for orders.

Done when:

  • Negative money and invalid quantities can't be constructed.
  • Illegal transitions (dispatching a cancelled order) throw with a clear message.
  • The order records domain events (OrderPlaced, OrderPaid, …) instead of calling other services.

docs.title: M2: Pricing (L1 to L2)
docs.text:
Build: a delivery fee rule (free from Rs 500, otherwise Rs 29), and coupon GREEN10: 10% off organic items when the basket is at least Rs 300 and contains organic items. Cache catalogue lookups.

Patterns: Strategy for fees, Specification for eligibility, Decorator for the caching catalogue.

Done when:

  • A new fee rule (members pay nothing) needs no change to checkout code.
  • Coupon conditions combine with and / or and are unit-tested separately.
  • Repeated catalogue lookups don't hit the database.

docs.title: M3: Delivery partners (L2 to L4)
docs.text:
Build: adapters for the QuickDrop and ParcelGo SDKs behind one DeliveryPartner interface; route by city; when ParcelGo fails, fall back to QuickDrop; after two consecutive ParcelGo failures, stop calling it (circuit open).

Patterns: Adapter, Factory Method for routing, circuit breaker and fallback from Resilience Patterns.

Done when:

  • Partner SDK types never leak outside the adapters.
  • With ParcelGo down, Pune orders still ship and ParcelGo stops receiving calls.

docs.title: M4: Checkout (L3 to L4)
docs.text:
Build: one checkout(idempotencyKey, order, coupon) entry point that reserves stock, charges PayLink, books delivery, and on any failure compensates in reverse (refund, release stock, cancel). The same key must never charge twice. Events are written to an outbox together with the state change and relayed to subscribers.

Patterns: Facade, saga and transactional outbox (Distributed Data Patterns), idempotency key (API Design Patterns), Observer for subscribers.

Done when:

  • A declined payment leaves stock unchanged and the order cancelled.
  • A failed delivery booking refunds the payment.
  • Retrying with the same key returns the same receipt without a second charge.
  • No event is published unless the state change is stored.

docs.title: M5: Mobile client contract (L3)
docs.text:
Build: one home-screen endpoint that aggregates what the app needs in a single call.

Patterns: aggregator / backend for frontend (UI and Mobile Patterns, Microservice Patterns).

Endpoint Method Purpose Notes /v1/home GET Loyalty points, recent orders, offers One call per screen /v1/checkout POST Place an order Requires Idempotency-Key header /v1/orders/{id} GET Order status Cacheable for 10 s /v1/orders?cursor= GET Order history Cursor pagination

Money is sent as integer totalPaise so the app never rounds floating-point values. Errors use Problem Details (application/problem+json).

Done when:

  • The app renders the home screen from one response.
  • Adding a field doesn't break older app versions (tolerant reader).

docs.title: M6: Production hardening (L4 to L5)
docs.text:
Build: replace the in-memory pieces with real infrastructure and add the checks from the Production Checklist.

  • Resilience4j instead of the hand-written breaker (Maven example).
  • Caffeine for the catalogue cache (Maven example).
  • ArchUnit rules for module boundaries (Maven example).
  • A real outbox table and relay (or CDC), and idempotent consumers.
  • Metrics, traces and alerts for checkout success rate and partner health.

docs.title: Reference solution
docs.text:
Try each milestone yourself first. The reference solution is a single runnable file, organised by milestone, so the whole flow fits on one screen of scrolling.

FreshCartCapstoneDemo.java
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.TreeMap;
import java.util.function.Consumer;
import java.util.function.Predicate;

/**
 * FreshCart capstone reference solution in one file. It wires together the patterns from the playbook: value
 * objects and an aggregate with State (M1), Strategy, Specification and a caching Decorator for pricing (M2),
 * Adapters, a Factory and a circuit breaker for delivery partners (M3), a checkout Facade running a saga with an
 * idempotency key and a transactional outbox (M4), Observer subscribers fed by the outbox relay, and an aggregated
 * home-screen contract for the mobile app (M5).
 */
public class FreshCartCapstoneDemo {

    // ===== M1: domain model =====
    record Money(long paise) implements Comparable<Money> {
        Money { if (paise < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("negative money"); }
        static Money rupees(long r) { return new Money(r * 100); }
        Money plus(Money o) { return new Money(paise + o.paise); }
        Money minus(Money o) { return new Money(Math.max(0, paise - o.paise)); }
        Money times(int n) { return new Money(paise * n); }
        Money percent(int p) { return new Money(paise * p / 100); }
        public int compareTo(Money o) { return Long.compare(paise, o.paise); }
        @Override public String toString() { return String.format("Rs %d.%02d", paise / 100, paise % 100); }
    }

    record Product(String sku, String name, Money price, Set<String> tags) {
        Product { tags = Set.copyOf(tags); }
    }

    record Line(Product product, int qty) {
        Line { if (qty < 1 || qty > 20) throw new IllegalArgumentException("quantity must be 1..20 for " + product.sku()); }
        Money total() { return product.price().times(qty); }
    }

    sealed interface OrderState permits Placed, Paid, Dispatched, Cancelled {
        default OrderState pay() { throw illegal("pay"); }
        default OrderState dispatch() { throw illegal("dispatch"); }
        default OrderState cancel() { throw illegal("cancel"); }
        private IllegalStateException illegal(String action) {
            return new IllegalStateException("cannot " + action + " an order that is " + getClass().getSimpleName().toUpperCase());
        }
    }
    record Placed() implements OrderState {
        public OrderState pay() { return new Paid(); }
        public OrderState cancel() { return new Cancelled(); }
    }
    record Paid() implements OrderState {
        public OrderState dispatch() { return new Dispatched(); }
        public OrderState cancel() { return new Cancelled(); }
    }
    record Dispatched() implements OrderState {}
    record Cancelled() implements OrderState {}

    record DomainEvent(String type, String orderId, String customer, String detail) {}

    static final class Order {
        final String id, customer, city;
        final List<Line> lines;
        private OrderState state = new Placed();
        private final List<DomainEvent> events = new ArrayList<>();

        Order(String id, String customer, String city, List<Line> lines) {
            if (lines.isEmpty()) throw new IllegalArgumentException("empty order");
            this.id = id; this.customer = customer; this.city = city; this.lines = List.copyOf(lines);
            events.add(new DomainEvent("OrderPlaced", id, customer, ""));
        }
        Money subtotal() { return lines.stream().map(Line::total).reduce(new Money(0), Money::plus); }
        OrderState state() { return state; }
        void markPaid(Money amount) { state = state.pay(); events.add(new DomainEvent("OrderPaid", id, customer, amount.toString())); }
        void markDispatched(String partner) { state = state.dispatch(); events.add(new DomainEvent("OrderDispatched", id, customer, partner)); }
        void cancel(String reason) { state = state.cancel(); events.add(new DomainEvent("OrderCancelled", id, customer, reason)); }
        List<DomainEvent> drainEvents() { var copy = List.copyOf(events); events.clear(); return copy; }
    }

    // ===== M2: pricing =====
    interface Catalogue { Product find(String sku); }

    static final class InMemoryCatalogue implements Catalogue {
        final Map<String, Product> products = new TreeMap<>();
        int lookups;
        public Product find(String sku) { lookups++; return products.get(sku); }
    }

    record CachingCatalogue(Catalogue inner, Map<String, Product> cache) implements Catalogue {       // Decorator
        CachingCatalogue(Catalogue inner) { this(inner, new HashMap<>()); }
        public Product find(String sku) { return cache.computeIfAbsent(sku, inner::find); }
    }

    interface DeliveryFeePolicy { Money fee(Money basket); }                                          // Strategy
    static final DeliveryFeePolicy STANDARD_FEE = b -> b.compareTo(Money.rupees(500)) >= 0 ? new Money(0) : Money.rupees(29);

    record Coupon(String code, Predicate<Order> eligible, int percentOffOrganic) {}                     // Specification
    static final Predicate<Order> BASKET_OVER_300 = o -> o.subtotal().compareTo(Money.rupees(300)) >= 0;
    static final Predicate<Order> HAS_ORGANIC = o -> o.lines.stream().anyMatch(l -> l.product().tags().contains("organic"));
    static final Coupon GREEN10 = new Coupon("GREEN10", BASKET_OVER_300.and(HAS_ORGANIC), 10);

    record Quote(Money subtotal, Money discount, Money deliveryFee, Money total) {}

    static Quote price(Order o, Coupon coupon, DeliveryFeePolicy fees) {
        Money discount = new Money(0);
        if (coupon != null && coupon.eligible().test(o)) {
            Money organic = o.lines.stream().filter(l -> l.product().tags().contains("organic")).map(Line::total).reduce(new Money(0), Money::plus);
            discount = organic.percent(coupon.percentOffOrganic());
        }
        Money afterDiscount = o.subtotal().minus(discount);
        Money fee = fees.fee(afterDiscount);
        return new Quote(o.subtotal(), discount, fee, afterDiscount.plus(fee));
    }

    // ===== M3: delivery partners =====
    interface DeliveryPartner { String name(); String book(String orderId); }

    static final class QuickDropApi { String createJob(String ref) { return "QD-" + ref; } }               // partner SDKs
    static final class ParcelGoApi {
        boolean down = true; int calls;
        Map<String, String> schedule(String ref) {
            calls++;
            if (down) throw new IllegalStateException("ParcelGo 503");
            return Map.of("awb", "PG-" + ref);
        }
    }

    record QuickDropAdapter(QuickDropApi api) implements DeliveryPartner {                               // Adapter
        public String name() { return "QuickDrop"; }
        public String book(String orderId) { return api.createJob(orderId); }
    }
    record ParcelGoAdapter(ParcelGoApi api) implements DeliveryPartner {
        public String name() { return "ParcelGo"; }
        public String book(String orderId) { return api.schedule(orderId).get("awb"); }
    }

    static final class CircuitBreaker {
        private final int threshold; private int failures; boolean open;
        CircuitBreaker(int threshold) { this.threshold = threshold; }
        <T> T call(java.util.function.Supplier<T> action) {
            if (open) throw new IllegalStateException("circuit open");
            try { T r = action.get(); failures = 0; return r; }
            catch (RuntimeException e) { if (++failures >= threshold) open = true; throw e; }
        }
    }

    static final class PartnerRouter {                                                                  // Factory + fallback
        final DeliveryPartner quickDrop, parcelGo;
        final CircuitBreaker parcelGoBreaker = new CircuitBreaker(2);
        PartnerRouter(DeliveryPartner quickDrop, DeliveryPartner parcelGo) { this.quickDrop = quickDrop; this.parcelGo = parcelGo; }

        DeliveryPartner primaryFor(String city) { return city.equals("Pune") ? parcelGo : quickDrop; }

        String[] book(Order o) {
            DeliveryPartner primary = primaryFor(o.city);
            if (primary == quickDrop) return new String[] {quickDrop.name(), quickDrop.book(o.id)};
            try {
                return new String[] {parcelGo.name(), parcelGoBreaker.call(() -> parcelGo.book(o.id))};
            } catch (RuntimeException e) {
                return new String[] {quickDrop.name() + " (fallback: " + e.getMessage() + ")", quickDrop.book(o.id)};
            }
        }
    }

    // ===== M4: checkout facade, saga, idempotency, outbox =====
    static final class Stock {
        final Map<String, Integer> units = new TreeMap<>();
        void reserve(Order o) {
            for (Line l : o.lines) if (units.getOrDefault(l.product().sku(), 0) < l.qty()) throw new IllegalStateException("out of stock: " + l.product().sku());
            o.lines.forEach(l -> units.merge(l.product().sku(), -l.qty(), Integer::sum));
        }
        void release(Order o) { o.lines.forEach(l -> units.merge(l.product().sku(), l.qty(), Integer::sum)); }
    }

    static final class PayLink {
        final List<String> ledger = new ArrayList<>();
        final Money limit = Money.rupees(2000);
        String charge(String orderId, Money amount) {
            if (amount.compareTo(limit) > 0) throw new IllegalStateException("PayLink declined " + amount);
            ledger.add("charge " + orderId + " " + amount);
            return "PL-" + orderId;
        }
        void refund(String paymentId, Money amount) { ledger.add("refund " + paymentId + " " + amount); }
    }

    record Receipt(String orderId, String status, Quote quote, String partner, String tracking, String note) {}

    static final class CheckoutFacade {
        final Stock stock; final PayLink payLink; final PartnerRouter partners;
        final Map<String, Receipt> idempotency = new HashMap<>();
        final List<DomainEvent> outbox = new ArrayList<>();

        CheckoutFacade(Stock stock, PayLink payLink, PartnerRouter partners) { this.stock = stock; this.payLink = payLink; this.partners = partners; }

        Receipt checkout(String idempotencyKey, Order order, Coupon coupon) {
            Receipt previous = idempotency.get(idempotencyKey);
            if (previous != null) return previous;
            Quote quote = price(order, coupon, STANDARD_FEE);
            Receipt receipt;
            String paymentId = null;
            boolean reserved = false;
            try {                                                                                     // saga steps
                stock.reserve(order); reserved = true;
                paymentId = payLink.charge(order.id, quote.total());
                order.markPaid(quote.total());
                String[] booking = partners.book(order);
                order.markDispatched(booking[0]);
                receipt = new Receipt(order.id, "DISPATCHED", quote, booking[0], booking[1], "");
            } catch (RuntimeException e) {                                                            // compensations in reverse
                if (paymentId != null) payLink.refund(paymentId, quote.total());
                if (reserved) stock.release(order);
                order.cancel(e.getMessage());
                receipt = new Receipt(order.id, "CANCELLED", quote, "-", "-", e.getMessage());
            }
            outbox.addAll(order.drainEvents());                                                       // same "transaction" as the state change
            idempotency.put(idempotencyKey, receipt);
            return receipt;
        }
    }

    static final class EventBus {                                                                       // Observer
        private final Map<String, List<Consumer<DomainEvent>>> subscribers = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        void subscribe(String type, Consumer<DomainEvent> s) { subscribers.computeIfAbsent(type, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(s); }
        void publish(DomainEvent e) { subscribers.getOrDefault(e.type(), List.of()).forEach(s -> s.accept(e)); }
    }

    static int relay(List<DomainEvent> outbox, EventBus bus) {
        int n = outbox.size();
        outbox.forEach(bus::publish);
        outbox.clear();
        return n;
    }

    // ===== M5: mobile home-screen contract =====
    static String homeScreenJson(String customer, int loyaltyPoints, List<Receipt> recent, List<Product> offers) {
        StringBuilder json = new StringBuilder("{\n  \"customer\": \"" + customer + "\",\n  \"loyaltyPoints\": " + loyaltyPoints + ",\n  \"recentOrders\": [");
        for (int i = 0; i < recent.size(); i++) {
            Receipt r = recent.get(i);
            json.append(i == 0 ? "\n" : ",\n").append("    {\"id\": \"").append(r.orderId()).append("\", \"status\": \"").append(r.status())
                .append("\", \"totalPaise\": ").append(r.quote().total().paise()).append("}");
        }
        json.append("\n  ],\n  \"offers\": [");
        for (int i = 0; i < offers.size(); i++) json.append(i == 0 ? "" : ", ").append('"').append(offers.get(i).name()).append('"');
        return json.append("]\n}").toString();
    }

    // ===== wiring and scenario =====
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        InMemoryCatalogue db = new InMemoryCatalogue();
        for (Product p : List.of(
                new Product("MILK-1L", "DairyDay Milk 1L", new Money(6800), Set.of("dairy")),
                new Product("CURD-500G", "DairyDay Curd 500g", new Money(4500), Set.of("dairy")),
                new Product("SPINACH-250G", "GreenValley Organic Spinach", new Money(6000), Set.of("organic", "vegetables")),
                new Product("RICE-5KG", "Basmati Rice 5kg", new Money(64000), Set.of("staples")))) db.products.put(p.sku(), p);
        Catalogue catalogue = new CachingCatalogue(db);
        Stock stock = new Stock();
        stock.units.putAll(Map.of("MILK-1L", 50, "CURD-500G", 30, "SPINACH-250G", 10, "RICE-5KG", 5));
        PayLink payLink = new PayLink();
        ParcelGoApi parcelGoApi = new ParcelGoApi();
        CheckoutFacade checkout = new CheckoutFacade(stock, payLink, new PartnerRouter(new QuickDropAdapter(new QuickDropApi()), new ParcelGoAdapter(parcelGoApi)));

        Map<String, Integer> points = new TreeMap<>();
        EventBus bus = new EventBus();
        bus.subscribe("OrderDispatched", e -> System.out.println("  TextBlast SMS to " + e.customer() + ": order " + e.orderId() + " is on its way with " + e.detail().split(" ")[0]));
        bus.subscribe("OrderPaid", e -> points.merge(e.customer(), 10, Integer::sum));
        bus.subscribe("OrderCancelled", e -> System.out.println("  TextBlast SMS to " + e.customer() + ": order " + e.orderId() + " cancelled, no charge"));

        System.out.println("M2 pricing and M4 checkout:");
        Order o1 = new Order("FC-1001", "asha", "Bengaluru", List.of(new Line(catalogue.find("MILK-1L"), 2),
                new Line(catalogue.find("SPINACH-250G"), 3), new Line(catalogue.find("CURD-500G"), 1)));
        Receipt r1 = checkout.checkout("key-asha-1", o1, GREEN10);
        System.out.println("  " + r1.orderId() + " " + r1.status() + " via " + r1.partner() + " " + r1.tracking() + ": subtotal " + r1.quote().subtotal()
                + ", GREEN10 -" + r1.quote().discount() + ", delivery " + r1.quote().deliveryFee() + ", total " + r1.quote().total());
        Receipt again = checkout.checkout("key-asha-1", o1, GREEN10);
        System.out.println("  retry with the same idempotency key returns the same receipt: " + (again == r1) + ", charges so far " + payLink.ledger.size());

        System.out.println("M3 partners in Pune (ParcelGo is down):");
        List<Receipt> pune = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) {
            Order o = new Order("FC-200" + i, "bilal", "Pune", List.of(new Line(catalogue.find("MILK-1L"), 1), new Line(catalogue.find("RICE-5KG"), 1)));
            Receipt r = checkout.checkout("key-bilal-" + i, o, null);
            pune.add(r);
            System.out.println("  " + r.orderId() + " " + r.status() + " via " + r.partner());
        }
        System.out.println("  ParcelGo was called " + parcelGoApi.calls + " times; breaker open = " + checkout.partners.parcelGoBreaker.open);

        System.out.println("M4 saga compensation:");
        Order big = new Order("FC-3001", "chen", "Bengaluru", List.of(new Line(catalogue.find("RICE-5KG"), 2), new Line(catalogue.find("MILK-1L"), 20)));
        Receipt rb = checkout.checkout("key-chen-1", big, null);
        System.out.println("  " + rb.orderId() + " " + rb.status() + ": " + rb.note() + "; rice stock back to " + stock.units.get("RICE-5KG") + ", milk " + stock.units.get("MILK-1L"));
        try {
            big.markDispatched("QuickDrop");
        } catch (IllegalStateException e) {
            System.out.println("  state guard: " + e.getMessage());
        }

        System.out.println("M4 outbox relay to subscribers:");
        int published = relay(checkout.outbox, bus);
        System.out.println("  published " + published + " events; loyalty points " + points);
        System.out.println("  PayLink ledger " + payLink.ledger);
        System.out.println("  catalogue lookups hitting the database: " + db.lookups + " (cache serves the rest)");

        System.out.println("M5 home screen contract for the mobile app:");
        List<Product> offers = db.products.values().stream().filter(p -> p.tags().contains("organic") || p.tags().contains("dairy")).toList();
        System.out.println(homeScreenJson("asha", points.getOrDefault("asha", 0), List.of(r1), offers));
    }
}

Run it: java FreshCartCapstoneDemo.java

M2 pricing and M4 checkout:
  FC-1001 DISPATCHED via QuickDrop QD-FC-1001: subtotal Rs 361.00, GREEN10 -Rs 18.00, delivery Rs 29.00, total Rs 372.00
  retry with the same idempotency key returns the same receipt: true, charges so far 1
M3 partners in Pune (ParcelGo is down):
  FC-2001 DISPATCHED via QuickDrop (fallback: ParcelGo 503)
  FC-2002 DISPATCHED via QuickDrop (fallback: ParcelGo 503)
  FC-2003 DISPATCHED via QuickDrop (fallback: circuit open)
  ParcelGo was called 2 times; breaker open = true
M4 saga compensation:
  FC-3001 CANCELLED: PayLink declined Rs 2640.00; rice stock back to 2, milk 45
  state guard: cannot dispatch an order that is CANCELLED
M4 outbox relay to subscribers:
  TextBlast SMS to asha: order FC-1001 is on its way with QuickDrop
  TextBlast SMS to bilal: order FC-2001 is on its way with QuickDrop
  TextBlast SMS to bilal: order FC-2002 is on its way with QuickDrop
  TextBlast SMS to bilal: order FC-2003 is on its way with QuickDrop
  TextBlast SMS to chen: order FC-3001 cancelled, no charge
  published 14 events; loyalty points {asha=10, bilal=30}
  PayLink ledger [charge FC-1001 Rs 372.00, charge FC-2001 Rs 708.00, charge FC-2002 Rs 708.00, charge FC-2003 Rs 708.00]
  catalogue lookups hitting the database: 4 (cache serves the rest)
M5 home screen contract for the mobile app:
{
  "customer": "asha",
  "loyaltyPoints": 10,
  "recentOrders": [
    {"id": "FC-1001", "status": "DISPATCHED", "totalPaise": 37200}
  ],
  "offers": ["DairyDay Curd 500g", "DairyDay Milk 1L", "GreenValley Organic Spinach"]
}

What to notice:

  • GREEN10 takes 10% of the organic spinach only (Rs 18.00 of Rs 180.00), and the delivery fee still applies because the basket is under Rs 500.
  • The second checkout with key-asha-1 returns the stored receipt; PayLink's ledger shows one charge.
  • ParcelGo was called twice; the third Pune order went straight to the fallback because the circuit was open.
  • The oversized order was declined by PayLink, and the saga put stock back exactly as it was.
  • Events were collected in the outbox during checkout and only reached SMS and loyalty when the relay ran.

docs.title: Tests
Assessing your solution
docs.text: Level What a good solution shows L1–L2 Correct value objects and state transitions, patterns used where they remove real duplication, unit tests per rule L3 Clear package boundaries, idempotent checkout, outbox, consistent error handling, an API contract the app team can use L4 Resilience tuned per partner, saga failure cases tested, observability, an explanation of consistency trade-offs L5 Architecture decision records, fitness functions, a plan to split into services only where boundaries are proven

docs.title: Stretch goals
docs.text:
• Split checkout, pricing and delivery into separate services with Kafka between them (Messaging Patterns).
  • Model the order with event sourcing and build an order-history projection (Distributed Data Patterns).
  • Add a supplier feed pipeline for DairyDay price updates with a content-based router and dead letter channel.
  • Migrate the legacy loyalty system with a strangler fig and parallel run (Legacy Modernisation).

docs.title: Anti-Pattern Catalogue
docs.text:
TL;DR

Every anti-pattern mentioned in the playbook, in one place: how to recognise it, why it hurts, and the fix, with a link to the page that explains it in depth. Use it as a review checklist.

How to use it. Scan the "Symptom" column during code or design review. An anti-pattern is a common response to a real problem that causes more harm than it removes, so each fix names the pattern or practice that solves the original problem better.

docs.title: Code-level smells
docs.text: Anti-pattern Symptom Why it hurts Fix Read more God class CheckoutService with 3,000 lines and 40 dependencies Every change conflicts; nobody understands it Extract classes by responsibility, Facade for callers Anti-Patterns and Code Smells Long parameter list quote(a, b, c, d, e, f, g) Wrong argument order, hard to evolve Parameter object or Builder Builder Primitive obsession Prices as double, SKUs as String everywhere Rounding bugs, mixed-up values Value objects (records) such as Money, Sku DDD Tactical Switch on type everywhere The same switch (type) in many classes Every new type means editing many places Strategy or polymorphism, or a sealed type with one exhaustive switch Strategy Feature envy A method uses another object's data more than its own Logic in the wrong place Move the method to the data Refactoring to Patterns Shotgun surgery One change touches ten files Slow, risky changes Gather the knowledge into one class or module SOLID Principles Null returns everywhere if (x != null) chains NullPointerExceptions, noise Optional for return values, Null Object for collaborators Null Object Swallowed exceptions catch (Exception e) {} Silent data corruption Handle, translate or rethrow; log once at the boundary Error Handling Patterns Exceptions for control flow try { parse } catch to test validity Slow, unclear Validation methods, result types Error Handling Patterns

docs.title: Cheat Sheet
docs.text:
TL;DR

Every pattern on one page: intent, when to reach for it, and a minimal Java 21 skeleton in the FreshCart domain. Follow the link on each name for the full deep dive with runnable examples.

How to read this page. Each entry has a one-line intent, a use when hint, and the smallest code that shows the structure. Skeletons are trimmed for scanning; the linked pages have complete, runnable versions.

docs.title: Singleton
docs.text:
Intent: exactly one instance, globally reachable. Use when: a truly single resource (a registry or config); prefer DI-managed singletons.

public enum PriceRegistry { INSTANCE; long priceOf(String sku) { return 6800; } }

docs.title: Factory Method
docs.text:
Intent: let a method decide which subclass to create. Use when: creation logic varies by input or subclass.

static Notifier notifierFor(Channel c) {
    return switch (c) { case SMS -> new SmsNotifier(); case PUSH -> new PushNotifier(); };
}

docs.title: Abstract Factory
docs.text:
Intent: create families of related objects without naming concrete classes. Use when: products must match (one partner's client + parser + signer).

interface PartnerKit { DeliveryClient client(); LabelPrinter printer(); }
final class QuickDropKit implements PartnerKit { /* QuickDrop implementations */ }

docs.title: Builder
docs.text:
Intent: construct complex objects step by step. Use when: many optional parameters, or validation across fields.

Order order = Order.builder().customer("C-17").item("MILK-1L", 2).slot("18:00-20:00").build();

docs.title: Prototype
docs.text:
Intent: create objects by copying a configured instance. Use when: construction is expensive or templates vary slightly.

record BasketTemplate(String name, List<String> skus) { BasketTemplate withName(String n) { return new BasketTemplate(n, skus); } }

docs.title: Object Pool
docs.text:
Intent: reuse expensive objects instead of creating them. Use when: creation is truly expensive (connections); not for ordinary objects.

HikariDataSource pool = new HikariDataSource(config);   // borrow with getConnection(), return with close()

docs.title: Adapter
docs.text:
Intent: make an incompatible interface fit the one you expect. Use when: integrating a partner or legacy API.

final class ParcelGoAdapter implements DeliveryClient {
    private final ParcelGoApi api;
    public Quote quote(Address a) { return Quote.ofRupees(api.getRate(a.pincode())); }
}

docs.title: Bridge
docs.text:
Intent: separate an abstraction from its implementation so both vary. Use when: two independent dimensions (notification type × channel).

abstract class Alert { protected final Channel channel; abstract void send(String user); }

docs.title: Composite
docs.text:
Intent: treat single objects and groups uniformly. Use when: tree structures (bundles of products, category menus).

sealed interface BasketItem permits Product, Bundle { long pricePaise(); }
record Bundle(List<BasketItem> items) implements BasketItem { public long pricePaise() { return items.stream().mapToLong(BasketItem::pricePaise).sum(); } }

docs.title: Decorator
docs.text:
Intent: add behaviour by wrapping, without subclassing. Use when: optional, stackable features (logging, caching, retries).

PriceService prices = new CachingPriceService(new LoggingPriceService(new DbPriceService()));

docs.title: Facade
docs.text:
Intent: a simple entry point to a complex subsystem. Use when: callers need one operation that spans many services.

final class CheckoutFacade { Receipt checkout(Cart c) { stock.reserve(c); var p = payments.charge(c); return orders.place(c, p); } }

docs.title: Flyweight
docs.text:
Intent: share immutable state across many objects. Use when: millions of similar objects (catalogue units, icons).

static final Map<String, Unit> UNITS = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
static Unit unit(String code) { return UNITS.computeIfAbsent(code, Unit::new); }

docs.title: Proxy
docs.text:
Intent: a stand-in that controls access to the real object. Use when: lazy loading, access control, remoting, caching.

final class LazyImageProxy implements ProductImage { private ProductImage real; public byte[] bytes() { if (real == null) real = load(); return real.bytes(); } }

docs.title: Strategy
docs.text:
Intent: interchangeable algorithms behind one interface. Use when: pricing, fees or routing rules vary.

interface DeliveryFee { long feePaise(long basketPaise); }
DeliveryFee standard = b -> b >= 50000 ? 0 : 2900;

docs.title: Observer
docs.text:
Intent: notify dependents when state changes. Use when: one event, many independent reactions.

orderEvents.subscribe(e -> sms.send(e.customer(), "Order " + e.id() + " placed"));

docs.title: Template Method
docs.text:
Intent: fixed algorithm skeleton, variable steps. Use when: several processes share structure.

abstract class ReportJob { final void run() { var d = load(); write(format(d)); } abstract List<Row> load(); abstract String format(List<Row> d); }

docs.title: Chain of Responsibility
docs.text:
Intent: pass a request along handlers until one handles it. Use when: validation or approval pipelines.

interface CouponRule { Optional<String> reject(Order o); }
rules.stream().map(r -> r.reject(order)).flatMap(Optional::stream).findFirst();

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
Intent: a request as an object. Use when: queueing, undo, retries, audit.

record AddItem(String sku, int qty) implements CartCommand { public void apply(Cart c) { c.add(sku, qty); } }

docs.title: Iterator
docs.text:
Intent: traverse without exposing internals. Use when: custom collections, paging through APIs.

final class OrderPages implements Iterable<Order> { public Iterator<Order> iterator() { return new PageIterator(api); } }

docs.title: Mediator
docs.text:
Intent: centralise interaction between objects. Use when: many components talk to each other (checkout screen widgets).

final class CheckoutMediator { void slotChanged(Slot s) { fee.recalculate(s); summary.refresh(); } }

docs.title: Memento
docs.text:
Intent: capture and restore state without breaking encapsulation. Use when: undo, drafts.

record CartSnapshot(Map<String, Integer> lines) {}
CartSnapshot s = cart.save(); cart.restore(s);

docs.title: State
docs.text:
Intent: behaviour changes with internal state. Use when: order lifecycles with rules per state.

sealed interface OrderState permits Placed, Packed, Delivered { OrderState next(); }

docs.title: Visitor
docs.text:
Intent: add operations to a fixed type hierarchy. Use when: many operations over stable types; in Java 21 often a pattern-matching switch.

long tax(BasketItem i) { return switch (i) { case Product p -> p.pricePaise() * 5 / 100; case Bundle b -> b.items().stream().mapToLong(this::tax).sum(); }; }

docs.title: Interpreter
docs.text:
Intent: evaluate sentences of a small language. Use when: rule or coupon expressions.

sealed interface Expr permits MinBasket, And { boolean eval(Order o); }

docs.title: Principles in one line each
docs.text:
Principle One line SRP One reason to change per class OCP Extend behaviour without editing tested code LSP Subtypes must keep the parent's promises ISP Small, client-specific interfaces DIP Depend on abstractions owned by the policy layer DRY / KISS / YAGNI Don't duplicate knowledge; keep it simple; don't build for imagined needs Rule of three Extract a pattern on the third real variation

See SOLID Principles and DRY, KISS, YAGNI and Friends.
